title: Optimizing AI Models for Inference
description: How to make trained AI models smaller, faster and cheaper to run: quantization, pruning, distillation, batching, compilers and runtimes, LLM tricks like the KV cache and speculative decoding, plus serving cost and how to verify nothing broke. Built for developers new to ML. Builds on this library's mlops course for the wider production lifecycle (registries, pipelines, monitoring) — see it for that foundation.

changelog.notes: Initial release — 31 decks, each pack with a preview card teaching the concept before its graded main card and practice cards, including scenario questions and packs on modern LLM serving topics.
Glossary: every term now points at one link, so the same word never sends you to two different pages.
One practice question named neither method it asked about; it now names GPTQ and AWQ.

Adds a Learn more article for every glossary term (43 articles, each with a worked example); tapping a term now offers "Read the full explanation". Glossary entries Outlier, Outliers, Ranks and Slices now have one meaning each, and two practice cards say "pieces" instead of "slices" and "scores" instead of "ranks".
Removes the Wikipedia links from glossary terms that have a Learn more article; the article is now the single place to read more.
Rewrites the Learn more articles in a warmer, teacher-to-student voice; no change to the content or the glossary.

Cards: review fixes. Every pack's planned keywords are now defined in its main card, preview statements are repeated in the main card, practice cards mention their topic, and a few cards no longer use terms taught later.

toc: What a Model Is: Weights and Tensors
